h1: What an SEO consultant does and when you need one
metaTitle: What Is an SEO Consultant? Role and Fees
metaDescription: An SEO consultant is a senior specialist who diagnoses and directs but rarely executes. The role, the Indian fee bands in INR, and when to hire one.
answer: An SEO consultant is a senior specialist you hire for diagnosis and direction rather than delivery. They audit, prioritise, brief your team and review the work — but they rarely write the content or ship the code. In India they typically charge ₹1,500–₹15,000 an hour, or ₹25,000–₹1,50,000 for a fixed-scope audit.
takeaways: You're buying a **decision**, not capacity. The value is the hour where someone tells you why 900 pages fell out of the index — not the forty hours of fixing that follows.
Consultant fees in India span a tenfold range because the title is unregulated. A two-year freelancer and a former head of SEO at a marketplace use the same word.
A consultant is the right purchase when you have people who can execute and no idea what to point them at. It's the wrong one when you have neither.
The most common way this money gets wasted: nobody is named as owner of the fix list before the audit is commissioned.

sections.h2: What you're actually buying: judgement, not production
body: An agency sells you capacity — hours, articles, links, a team that shows up every month. A consultant sells you a decision. That difference explains almost everything else about how the two are priced and where each one fails.

Consider a real shape of problem: organic traffic drops 40% over six weeks and nobody knows why. An agency's answer is a retainer that starts with an audit and continues for a year. A consultant's answer is two days of work and a call in which someone says: your last release added a canonical rule to the category template, here are the 900 URLs it affected, here's the fix, here's how to verify it in Search Console. Same diagnosis. Very different invoice.

The catch is what happens next. The consultant hands you a correct list. Somebody still has to write the code, publish the pages and chase the approvals. If you don't have those people, you've bought an expensive document.

body: These get compared as if they're competing quotes for the same thing. They aren't. They solve different shortages.

sections.h2: What it costs in India, and why the range is so wide
body: Two honest caveats before the numbers. First, these are observed market ranges from the Indian agency and freelance market, not a survey — treat them as orientation, not a price list. Second, the range is enormous because "SEO consultant" is an unregulated title. Nothing stops a two-year freelancer and a former in-house head of SEO from using it on the same day.

bullets: **Seniority drives the hourly rate more than anything else.** You're paying for pattern recognition across sites you'll never see.
**Consultants billing international clients price their INR work off that.** A consultant charging USD 150/hr in the UK does not quote ₹2,000/hr in Mumbai.
**Audit price scales with URLs and stack.** A 40-page WordPress site and a 200,000-SKU headless catalogue are not the same job, and any consultant quoting the same fee for both hasn't looked.

callout.title: The audit that dies in a drawer
callout.body: Before you commission one, name the person who will own the fix list and state the sprint capacity they'll get. An audit with no owner is a ₹1,00,000 PDF, and it's the most common way this budget is wasted. If nobody can be named, buy execution instead.

sections.h2: What a consultant will not do
body: None of this is a criticism. It's the definition of the product, and misunderstanding it is where the disappointment comes from.
bullets: **Write your content.** Some will brief it or edit a draft. Almost none will produce four publishable pages a month — that's a content function, not a consulting one.
**Ship code.** They'll specify the fix precisely and review the pull request. Your engineers merge it.
**Do outreach.** Link acquisition is relationship work at volume. That's an agency or an in-house PR function, and it's the category consultants most reliably don't cover.

**Own the number.** A consultant advises. Accountability for organic performance stays with whoever inside your company signs off — see [who owns SEO inside a company](/answers/who-is-responsible-for-seo-in-a-company).

**Be available in week nine when something breaks** — unless you bought a retainer that says so. Project fees buy defined access, not availability. This is the most common surprise, and it's always in the contract.

sections.h2: When direction is genuinely all you need
body: Four situations where a consultant is clearly the right purchase, and one where it clearly isn't.
numbered: **You already have executors.** Writers, a dev team with real capacity, someone who can own a plan. What's missing is knowing what to point them at.
**The problem is diagnostic.** Traffic fell and nobody can explain it. Diagnosis is the highest-value hour in SEO and the one most worth buying from someone senior.
**There's a one-off event with a deadline.** A replatform, a domain change, a penalty, an international rollout. These need expertise for six weeks, not twelve months.

**You're about to commit serious budget.** A ₹50,000 audit before signing a ₹12,00,000 annual retainer is cheap insurance, and it makes you a much harder client to sell nonsense to. It also makes [comparing SEO proposals](/answers/how-to-compare-seo-proposals) far less guesswork.
bullets: The inverse: if you have no writers, no developer capacity and no internal owner, a consultant will hand you a correct plan you cannot act on. That's when you buy execution — an agency, or [SEO consulting with delivery attached](/services/seo-consulting).

sections.h2: How to brief a consultant so you get your money's worth
body: You're paying by the hour or for a fixed scope. Either way, the preparation you do beforehand converts directly into value.
numbered: **Send access before the first call.** Search Console, GA4, CMS read access, staging URL, existing keyword list. An hour spent waiting for logins is an hour you paid for.
**State the decision you need made, not the topic.** "Should we move the blog from a subdomain to a subfolder before the redesign?" beats "can you review our SEO?" by an order of magnitude.
**Say what you can actually ship.** If your developers have two hours a month, say so up front. A plan sized to their capacity and not the consultant's ideal is the one that gets built.

**Give them the change log.** Past migrations, penalties, agency changes, big releases, with dates. Most "mystery" traffic drops are explained by something in that list, and finding it yourself costs you nothing.
**Agree the deliverable format in advance.** A prioritised ticket list your team can pick up on Monday beats a 60-slide deck every time. Ask for it in the format your team already works in.
**Book the follow-up in the same contract.** Sixty minutes, two weeks after delivery, to answer the questions that only appear during implementation. It's the cheapest hour in the engagement.

faqs.q: What's the difference between an SEO consultant and an SEO agency?
faqs.a: A consultant sells diagnosis and direction; an agency sells capacity to execute. Hire a consultant when you have a team and no plan. Hire an agency when you have a plan and nobody to run it. Buying the wrong one wastes a quarter.

faqs.q: How much does an SEO consultant charge in India?
faqs.a: Broadly ₹1,500–₹15,000 an hour, or ₹25,000–₹1,50,000 for a fixed-scope technical audit. The range is wide because the title is unregulated and audit price tracks site size. Ask what the fee covers in hours before comparing two quotes.

faqs.q: Is an SEO consultant worth it for a small business?
faqs.a: Often yes, and cheaper than a retainer. A few hours with someone senior can point a small team at the right ten things. It stops being worth it when nobody internally has time to do the work afterwards.

Almost never, and honestly they shouldn't — they don't control execution. Anyone guaranteeing a ranking position is guaranteeing something nobody controls. A guarantee only makes sense when the same party owns both the plan and the delivery.

faqs.q: How long should an SEO consulting engagement last?
faqs.a: A diagnostic audit is two to four weeks. A strategy sprint is four to six. Advisory retainers work well as rolling monthly arrangements with a few hours each. If a consulting engagement is quoted at twelve months, you're buying an agency with a different label.

faqs.q: Can an SEO consultant work alongside my existing agency?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's one of the more useful arrangements — an independent reviewer checking the agency's priorities and output quality. Tell both sides it's happening. A consultant brought in secretly produces defensiveness rather than better work.
